description: This topic explores the meaning and components of Tanzanian culture, the difference between material and non-material culture, why preserving culture matters, and how cultural change and globalization affect Tanzanian society.

mcq.questionText: What is the most accurate meaning of culture?

options.text: The total way of life of a group of people, including their beliefs, customs and practices
Only the traditional dances performed during national festivals
The money and property owned by a community
The natural environment in which people live

mcq.explanation: Culture refers to the entire way of life of a society, covering beliefs, customs, values and practices passed from one generation to the next.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an example of MATERIAL culture?

options.text: Respect for elders
A traditional drum used in dances
Belief in ancestors
The Swahili language

mcq.explanation: Material culture consists of physical objects made by people, such as drums, tools, clothes and buildings.

mcq.questionText: Which national language unites Tanzanians from different ethnic groups?

options.text: English
French
Kiswahili
Arabic

mcq.explanation: Kiswahili is the national language of Tanzania and is a strong unifying element of Tanzanian culture.

mcq.questionText: Norms in a society can best be described as:

options.text: Physical tools used in daily work
Accepted rules and standards that guide how people behave
Foreign goods imported into the country
The total population of a community

mcq.explanation: Norms are the shared rules and expectations that guide acceptable behaviour within a society.

mcq.questionText: Which of these is a component of NON-material culture?

options.text: Traditional clothing
Cooking pots
Values such as honesty and respect
Wood carvings

mcq.explanation: Non-material culture includes ideas, values, beliefs and customs that cannot be touched, such as honesty and respect.

mcq.questionText: Why is preserving culture important for a nation like Tanzania?

options.text: It helps maintain identity and unity among the people
It increases the number of foreign languages spoken
It removes all traditional customs
It stops people from communicating

mcq.explanation: Preserving culture keeps a nation's identity alive and strengthens unity and a sense of belonging among its people.

mcq.questionText: Globalization mainly affects Tanzanian culture by:

options.text: Completely stopping the use of mobile phones
Introducing foreign ideas, dress and music that may replace local ones
Forcing everyone to wear only traditional clothes
Reducing the number of countries in the world

mcq.explanation: Globalization spreads foreign influences such as dress, music and food, which can sometimes weaken or replace local cultural practices.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best represents Tanzanian traditional art?

options.text: Makonde wood carvings
Imported plastic toys
Computer games
Foreign cartoons

mcq.explanation: Makonde wood carvings are a well-known form of traditional Tanzanian art that expresses the community's skills and heritage.

mcq.questionText: Beliefs as a component of culture refer to:

options.text: Physical houses people build
Ideas that people accept as true, such as religious or spiritual convictions
The roads connecting towns
Money used for trade

mcq.explanation: Beliefs are ideas that people hold to be true, including religious, spiritual and traditional convictions that shape their behaviour.

options.text: Long-established ways of doing things passed from generation to generation
Brand new inventions made each year
Laws made only by foreign countries
Tools used for farming

mcq.explanation: Customs are traditional and accepted ways of behaving that a community follows and passes down over time.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is a popular Tanzanian traditional food?

options.text: Ugali
Pizza
Hamburger
Sushi

mcq.explanation: Ugali, made from maize flour, is a staple traditional food widely eaten across Tanzania.

mcq.questionText: Values within a culture are best understood as:

options.text: Prices of goods in the market
Principles and standards that a society considers important and good
Buildings used for worship
Imported electronic devices

mcq.explanation: Values are the deeply held principles, such as honesty, hard work and respect, that a society regards as desirable and good.

mcq.questionText: A negative effect of cultural change on Tanzanian youth may be:

options.text: Learning to read and write
Abandoning respectful customs and adopting harmful foreign habits
Speaking Kiswahili more often
Eating traditional foods

mcq.explanation: Cultural change can be negative when young people abandon good customs and values and copy harmful foreign behaviours.

mcq.questionText: Traditional dances in Tanzanian culture are mainly used to:

options.text: Replace the national flag
Express community feelings and celebrate important occasions
Pay taxes to the government
Build roads and bridges

mcq.explanation: Traditional dances are used to express joy, celebrate occasions such as weddings and harvests, and pass on cultural messages.

mcq.questionText: Which one of the following is the BEST way to preserve Tanzanian culture?

options.text: Ignoring traditional languages and customs
Teaching young people about their traditions and protecting cultural sites
Replacing all local foods with foreign foods
Stopping the use of Kiswahili

mcq.explanation: Culture is best preserved by educating the young generation about their heritage and by protecting cultural sites and practices.

fib.explanation: Culture is the complete way of life of a people, including their beliefs, customs and practices.

fib.questionText: Physical objects made by people, such as tools and clothing, are part of _____ culture.
fib.explanation: Material culture refers to tangible items created by a society.

fib.questionText: Ideas, values and beliefs that cannot be touched belong to _____ culture.
fib.explanation: Non-material culture includes intangible elements such as values, beliefs and customs.

fib.questionText: The national language that unites Tanzanians is _____.
fib.explanation: Kiswahili serves as a common language uniting people of different ethnic groups in Tanzania.

fib.questionText: Accepted rules that guide how people should behave in society are called _____.
fib.explanation: Norms are shared standards of acceptable behaviour in a community.

fib.questionText: Long-established ways of doing things that are passed down through generations are known as _____.
fib.explanation: Customs are traditional practices handed down from one generation to the next.

fib.questionText: A staple traditional Tanzanian food made from maize flour is _____.
fib.explanation: Ugali is a common staple food eaten throughout Tanzania.

fib.questionText: The spread of foreign ideas, goods and lifestyles across the world is called _____.
fib.explanation: Globalization links countries and spreads cultural influences worldwide.

fib.questionText: Principles such as honesty and respect that a society considers important are called _____.
fib.explanation: Values are the cherished principles that guide a society's sense of right and wrong.

fib.questionText: Famous Tanzanian wood carvings produced by the Makonde people are an example of traditional _____.
fib.explanation: Makonde carvings are a recognized form of Tanzanian traditional art.

tf.questionText: Culture includes the language, customs, beliefs and values of a group of people.
tf.explanation: Language, customs, beliefs and values are all components of culture.

tf.questionText: A traditional drum is an example of non-material culture.
tf.explanation: A drum is a physical object, so it is part of material culture, not non-material culture.

tf.questionText: Kiswahili helps to unite Tanzanians from different ethnic backgrounds.
tf.explanation: Kiswahili is a national language that promotes unity among diverse ethnic groups.

tf.questionText: Preserving culture is unimportant and brings no benefit to a nation.
tf.explanation: Preserving culture is important because it maintains identity, unity and a sense of belonging.

tf.questionText: Globalization can sometimes weaken local Tanzanian cultural practices.
tf.explanation: Foreign influences brought by globalization can replace or weaken local customs and practices.

tf.questionText: Values and beliefs are examples of material culture.
tf.explanation: Values and beliefs cannot be touched, so they belong to non-material culture.

tf.questionText: Traditional dances are used to celebrate occasions and express community feelings.
tf.explanation: Dances express joy and mark important events such as weddings and harvests.

tf.questionText: Customs are brand new practices invented every year by the government.
tf.explanation: Customs are long-established practices passed down through generations, not new yearly inventions.

tf.questionText: Teaching young people about their traditions helps to preserve culture.
tf.explanation: Educating the youth about heritage is one of the best ways to keep culture alive.

tf.questionText: All cultural change is harmful and brings no positive effects.
tf.explanation: Cultural change can also be positive, for example through education, technology and abandoning harmful practices.

hoq.questionText: A village elder complains that young people no longer greet elders properly, prefer foreign music, and rarely use traditional foods. Which conclusion best explains this situation?

options.text: It shows cultural change caused largely by globalization and foreign influence
It proves the youth have lost the ability to speak any language
It means the village has no culture at all
It shows that material culture has completely disappeared

hoq.explanation: The changes in greetings, music and food reflect cultural change driven by globalization and the adoption of foreign influences.

hoq.questionText: Two communities both value respect, but one expresses it by kneeling while the other expresses it by bowing. What does this best illustrate about culture?

options.text: That respect is part of material culture
That a shared value can be shown through different customs in different cultures
That only one of the communities truly has values
That values and customs mean exactly the same thing

hoq.explanation: A common value such as respect (non-material) can be expressed through different customs, showing how values and practices relate yet differ across cultures.

hoq.questionText: A government decides to record traditional songs, document local languages, and protect historical sites. Which statement BEST evaluates this decision?

options.text: It is wasteful because culture has no value
It is a wise effort to preserve cultural heritage and strengthen national identity
It will force all citizens to abandon Kiswahili
It only protects material culture and ignores everything else

hoq.explanation: Recording songs and languages and protecting sites preserves both material and non-material heritage, strengthening identity and unity for future generations.
